A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same joint-group-equivariant universality framework. All 17 pages of v4 and 19 pages of v5, including figures, equations and appendices, support comparison; retained material can be matched across renumbering and reformatting.

before.justification: V4 contains mathematical constructions, universality theorems and proofs, including Appendix A. Its architecture examples are theoretical, with no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V5 remains theoretical throughout the main text and Appendices A–E. The added approximation and representation-theoretic results are mathematical proofs, not original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The joint-equivariant machines, deep ridgelet formulas and fully connected, convolutional and quadratic network constructions are unchanged. Appendix C supplies a finite-approximation argument for the existing integral model without revising the proposed learning procedure or architecture.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. The added shallow-network example in Appendix B is a mathematical illustration, not additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed framework. The expanded discussion of classical approximation proofs does not introduce experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No experimental splits, metrics, budgets, sample sizes or testing procedures are reported in either version. The new appendices introduce mathematical hypotheses rather than evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments or empirical case studies. The additional appendix arguments concern mathematical approximation and operator properties.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates and significance tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical performance values, rankings or observed result entries. The newly reported mathematical results belong under T1.

T1.justification: V5 adds a shallow-network derivation in Appendix B, a conditional uniform approximation theorem for finite networks in Appendix C, boundedness and composition lemmas in Appendix D, and affine-group irreducibility proofs in Appendix E. This substantially expands the formal support beyond v4's Appendix A. The main reconstruction theorem, v4 Theorem 4/v5 Theorem 3.10, and the retained Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same universality theorem and four applications. The added concluding discussion extends the claimed significance to nonvector settings and pessimistic depth-dependent generalization analysis, without adding a generalization theorem.

C2.justification: Section 8 adds an explanation linking pessimistic generalization bounds to coarse Lipschitz estimates and argues for the interpretability of ridgelet-based approximation. Remark C.5 additionally explains the roles of compact parameter spaces, finite measures and Lipschitz continuity in discretization. The central interpretation of universality through irreducibility is retained.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation instructions, experimental hyperparameters, hardware, training times or code/data access information. The added appendices document mathematical constructions and proofs.

R1.justification: V5 adds supporting references to Evans and Gariepy, Kainen et al., Kobayashi and Oshima, Lang, and Yosida. Section 8 also expands the comparison with classical universality proof techniques. The existing related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. V5 expands the title, updates affiliations and acknowledgements, reorganizes the theorem remarks, adds explanatory and significance text plus an impact statement, and extends the appendix structure. The changes do not constitute extensive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference format, substantially reflowing text and equations and redesigning the title and author block. Figures 1 and 2 retain their content but are reduced and repositioned; appendices use full-width pages. Neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: Appendices B, C and E make v5 more self-contained and add a conditional connection between integral models and finite networks. However, the new Lemma D.1 proof, case T2, unjustifiably bounds a squared integral by the integral of the squared integrand. Appendix C also leaves its compactness and Lipschitz assumptions unconnected to the main network examples. These benefits and unresolved proof/applicability issues prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
